note: RFC 6793 §4.1 states: 'A NEW BGP speaker that receives the AS4_PATH attribute or the AS4_AGGREGATOR attribute in an UPDATE message from another NEW BGP speaker MUST discard the path attribute and continue processing the UPDATE message.' Section 6 repeats that sentence; its following logging SHOULD is a separate obligation, not silently included in this verdict. Re-read the primary passages, summary and unannotated checklist row, all three tagged covers, ReconcileASPathFamily and the actual receive preparation/rewrite/publication consumers. TestRFC6793NewSpeakerAS4AttributesAreDiscarded feeds both attributes with SourceASN4=true, requires successful reconciliation, exact unchanged canonical AS_PATH and AGGREGATOR, and exactly the discard codes [AttrAS4Path,AttrAS4Aggregator]. Its AS_PATH and AS4_PATH values agree, so that value equality alone does not distinguish a mistaken merge; the explicit discard assertions and the live AS4_PATH carrier supply the missing distinction. That carrier deliberately disagrees on the path tail and requires the complete relayed frame containing the original AS_PATH, ORIGIN, NEXT_HOP and announced prefix, with no AS4_PATH: retaining it, substituting its tail, dropping the UPDATE or treating its route as withdrawn cannot satisfy the expectation. TestRFC6793ReceivedAS4PathAcceptedAlongsideASPath supplies the OLD-source control and requires the AS4_PATH's non-mappable AS to become canonical instead of retaining AS_TRANS. The unit cover establishes both attribute decisions; the CI tagged to this ID establishes continued route processing and non-substitution end to end for AS4_PATH only, not an AS4_AGGREGATOR-specific end-to-end claim. Source inspection confirms the shared AS4FamilyPlan.WriteTo dispatch explicitly drops both legacy attributes, preserves unrelated attributes and NLRI, and returns the rewritten WireUpdate for normal callback publication. The separately tagged AS4_AGGREGATOR carrier under RFC6793-4.1-6 corroborates that same writer boundary but is not misrepresented as a tagged cover of this ID. Whole-producer halts remain reachability evidence, not selective discard proof. The combined tagged unit and functional assertions enforce both discard and continued-processing obligations.
